katas.title: Refunds: validate the amount up front, before entering the payment lock

provenance.find: L2 — Refund amount check is not concurrency-safe.

defects.scenario: Two POST /api/payments/:id/refund requests for 60 units arrive concurrently on a 100-unit payment.
defects.find: // Validate up front, before taking the lock: an over-limit request is rejected
defects.consequence: Both requests read refundedAmount = 0 before either refund row is written, both pass assertRefundAllowed, and 120 units end up refunded on a 100-unit capture. The check-then-act now runs outside the region the lock serializes — exactly finding L2's race, re-created one refactor later.

defects.scenario: The shipped service reads and asserts before the transaction opens at refundService.ts:36, and the schema has no constraint bounding the refund sum.
defects.consequence: Production has this same double-spend today: two concurrent 60-unit refunds on a 100-unit payment both become SUCCEEDED (reproduced as scratch checks C9/C10). The guide's fix shape — SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside the transaction, recompute the sum there — is what the kata's lock models.

tests.name: two concurrent 60-unit refunds on a 100-unit payment cannot both succeed (finding L2, scratch checks C9/C10)
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryPaymentStore({ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }); const svc = mod.createRefundService(store); const results = await Promise.allSettled([ svc.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 60, reason: 'damaged item' }), svc.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 60, reason: 'late delivery' }), ]); const succeeded = results.filter((r) => r.status === 'fulfilled'); assert.equal(succeeded.length, 1); const refunded = await store.sumSuccessfulRefundsForPayment('pay-1'); assert.ok(refunded <= 100, `refunded ${refunded} exceeds the 100-unit capture`);

tests.name: a sequential over-limit refund is still rejected with REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_CAPTURE
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryPaymentStore({ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'SUCCEEDED' }); const svc = mod.createRefundService(store); await svc.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 60, reason: 'partial' }); await assert.rejects(() => svc.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 60, reason: 'too much' }), (err) => err.code === 'REFUND_AMOUNT_EXCEEDS_CAPTURE');

tests.name: a refund on a non-succeeded payment is rejected
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryPaymentStore({ id: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 100, status: 'PENDING' }); const svc = mod.createRefundService(store); await assert.rejects(() => svc.createRefundForPayment({ paymentId: 'pay-1', amountMinor: 10, reason: 'x' }), (err) => err.code === 'PAYMENT_NOT_REFUNDABLE');

katas.title: Webhook dispatcher: list pending deliveries up front and mark them when done

provenance.find: No claim/lock, so two concurrent clicks process the same rows

defects.scenario: Two admins click "Deliver pending" at the same moment (or one admin double-clicks the button).
defects.consequence: Both dispatcher runs list the same PENDING rows before either marks one DELIVERED, so every webhook is processed twice — duplicate payment-status mutations that the inbound dedupe then has to absorb, and doubled attempt counts. The select and the status flip must be one atomic claim.

defects.scenario: The shipped dispatcher works from an unclaimed read-only listing.
defects.consequence: Trace D row D2 records exactly this: listPendingWebhookDeliveries filters status PENDING only (webhookRepository.ts:29-37) with no claim, and markWebhookDeliveryDelivered runs only after processProviderWebhook has already re-run, so two concurrent run-pending calls double-deliver every row.

tests.name: two concurrent dispatcher runs deliver each pending webhook exactly once (Trace D, row D2)
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryDeliveryStore([ { id: 'del-1', payload: { providerEventId: 'evt-1' } }, { id: 'del-2', payload: { providerEventId: 'evt-2' } }, ]); const processed = []; const processProviderWebhook = async (payload) => { processed.push(payload.providerEventId); }; const [first, second] = await Promise.all([ mod.deliverPendingWebhooks(store, processProviderWebhook, 10), mod.deliverPendingWebhooks(store, processProviderWebhook, 10), ]); assert.equal(processed.length, 2, `each webhook must be processed once, got ${processed.length} executions`); assert.equal(first.delivered + second.delivered, 2); assert.deepEqual([...new Set(processed)].sort(), ['evt-1', 'evt-2']);

tests.name: a failing delivery is marked FAILED with the error and the rest still deliver
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryDeliveryStore([ { id: 'del-1', payload: { providerEventId: 'evt-1' } }, { id: 'del-2', payload: { providerEventId: 'evt-2' } }, ]); const processProviderWebhook = async (payload) => { if (payload.providerEventId === 'evt-1') throw new Error('provider 500'); }; const out = await mod.deliverPendingWebhooks(store, processProviderWebhook, 10); assert.equal(out.delivered, 1); assert.equal(out.failed, 1); assert.equal(store.deliveries.find((d) => d.id === 'del-1').status, 'FAILED'); assert.equal(store.deliveries.find((d) => d.id === 'del-1').lastError, 'provider 500');

tests.name: the limit caps how many rows one run takes
tests.code: const store = new mod.InMemoryDeliveryStore([{ id: 'a', payload: {} }, { id: 'b', payload: {} }, { id: 'c', payload: {} }]); const out = await mod.deliverPendingWebhooks(store, async () => {}, 2); assert.equal(out.delivered, 2); assert.equal(store.deliveries.filter((d) => d.status === 'PENDING').length, 1);
